paper.title: RoboPhD: Evolving Diverse Complex Agents Under Tight Evaluation Budgets

gap.author_gap: Under tight evaluation budgets, validate-then-select (GEPA, Autoresearch) spends many evaluations on validation that do not help the next candidate (7-13 validated candidates per 1,500 budget), and there is no controlled head-to-head of the new artifact-evolution systems.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and quantified: validation sweeps consume most of the budget, and the authors show shrinking validation 200->100 helps all eight paired baseline results; the assumption that held-out validation is needed for reliable selection is the audited premise.
gap.lineage: OPRO/APE/DSPy prompt optimization -> GEPA (reflective Pareto, optimize_anything with ASI) -> Autoresearch (single-session greedy) -> RoboPhD (Elo tournament, validation-free, self-instrumentation). AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve target single-instance problems.
gap.closest_adjacent: GEPA and Autoresearch are directly compared; population-based noisy-fitness methods (successive halving, bandit allocation, quality-diversity archives) are not discussed.
gap.residue: Selection reliability per evaluation dollar; generalization of evolved artifacts.
gap.stakes: Up to $375 API cost per ARC run; human-judgment evaluations.
gap.method_response: Spend all evaluations on competition that doubles as evolution signal, with Elo accumulating weak selection signal.
gap.remaining_gap: Isolation of validation-free selection from other system differences; single-run variance; evolution-side cost; meta-evolution untested.
unresolved: GEPA and Autoresearch source/papers are not pinned locally, so the baselines' faithful configuration cannot be checked; noisy-selection/bandit literature as nearest neighbor is not discussed in the paper.

The mechanism's distinct prediction vs a no-tournament greedy control is only weakly borne out (KotH close).

X.reason: Algorithm 1 gives competitor selection, Elo constants, sample size, clone penalty, tie handling, Deep Focus and strategy prompt; failure handling of broken agents, versioning of the evolution session state and rollback rules beyond the AI's judgment are not specified.

E.measurement.reason: Four established benchmarks with executable or exact-match scoring, enforced cost caps and breach rates, separate test sets; the evaluator-gaming episode is disclosed and fixed. The ARC and BIRD benchmarks may be contaminated for the evolution model and the cost penalty is a 10% soft discount.

E.causality.reason: Useful controls (matched KotH, Deep Focus ablation, validation-size sweep on baselines), but engines differ in proposer channel, sampling and tooling, there is no run isolating validation-free selection, no ablation of the diversity mechanisms or self-instrumentation, and the authors concede the advantage over Autoresearch largely comes from shared features.

E.holdout.reason: Selection uses fresh training samples only and test sets are never used in optimization, identical across engines; baselines' validation size was chosen from two values on test scores (favoring baselines). Development of RoboPhD on Text2SQL and possible model contamination are not audited.

E.statistics.reason: Test sizes and losses (Can't Be Late) are reported, and the selection-noise simulation is exact, but every comparison is a single run without intervals or seeds, with a 2.2-point gap on DocFinQA and 'all eight paired' improvements from single runs.

E.cost.reason: Evaluation budget is the explicit matched resource with per-problem solver cost caps and breach rate reported; the evolution agent's own token/time cost, which differs sharply between Claude Code sessions and API reflection, is not reported.
